api: Canva API for integration and automation.
cons: Free and enterprise tiers coexist with different data terms
name: Canva AI
pros: AI in a tool most teams already use without a learning curve
files: Images, presentation files, and design assets in Canva's format.
value: AI-powered image generation, background removal, text effects, and presentation assistance inside the design tool most non-designer teams already use. The value is accessibility rather than frontier quality.
engine: Mix of Canva's own models and third-party providers. Text to image uses Stability AI and others.
latency: Fast enough for interactive design work.

pricing.includes: Higher credit allowances, brand kit, admin controls

quality: Sufficient for internal use and social content. Below the specialist tools for fine art or production-quality commercial imagery.
tagline: AI design features embedded in the tool most marketing and operations teams already use.
use_cases: Generating images and backgrounds for marketing collateral without a designer
Expanding, removing, or replacing image backgrounds in existing assets
Accelerating slide and social content production for marketing teams
governance_note: Two practical points. First, the training-provenance question follows the sub-processor, not just Canva: if the underlying image model carries provenance uncertainty, that uncertainty applies to your published assets. Second, the free tier has different data terms than the enterprise tier, and in many organizations both are in use simultaneously, with different staff operating under different agreements without knowing it.
training_optout: Canva's terms and its sub-processors' terms both apply. The training-data provenance of the image generation models it uses is inherited from those providers. Enterprise agreements provide stronger data controls.
